claims.text: What the image looks like String sign (terminal ileum narrowing) → Crohn disease
claims.quote: String sign (terminal ileum narrowing) Crohn disease

claims.text: Buzzword: string sign of Kantor (SBFT / CT enterography) = Crohn disease (terminal ileum)
claims.quote: String sign of Kantor SBFT / CT enterography Crohn disease (terminal ileum)

claims.text: Upper GI / barium enema: string sign of Kantor (terminal ileum) → Crohn disease
claims.quote: String sign of Kantor (terminal ileum) → Crohn disease

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Less acute presentation: MR or CT enterography (high-resolution imaging with large volumes of ingested contrast) are the procedures of choice; virtually diagnostic if they show characteristic strictures or fistulas with separation of bowel loops; an upper GI series with small-bowel follow-through is an alternative when these are unavailable
claims.quote: If initial presentation is less acute, MR and CT enterography, both of which combine high-resolution CT or MR imaging with large volumes of ingested contrast, are the procedures of choice (1, 2). These imaging studies are virtually diagnostic if they show characteristic strictures or fistulas with accompanying separation of bowel loops. An upper GI series with small-bowel follow-through and spot films of the terminal ileum is preferred over conventional CT and is an alternative approach when these advanced imaging techniques are unavailable.

claims.text: Upper GI / barium enema studies are largely replaced by colonoscopy and CT enterography in practice
claims.quote: Largely replaced by colonoscopy and CT enterography in practice

claims.text: Acute abdomen (at presentation or in a relapse): abdominal CT, which may show obstruction, abscesses or fistulas, or other causes (eg, appendicitis)
claims.quote: Patients presenting with an acute abdomen (either initially or during a relapse) should have an abdominal CT scan. These studies may show obstruction, abscesses or fistulas, and other possible causes of an acute abdomen (eg, appendicitis).

claims.text: Barium enema may be used if symptoms seem mainly colonic and may show reflux of barium into the terminal ileum with irregularity, nodularity, stiffness, wall thickening and a narrowed lumen; similar findings: cecal cancer, ileal carcinoid, lymphoma, systemic vasculitis, radiation enteritis, ileocecal tuberculosis, ameboma
claims.quote: Barium enema radiograph may be used if symptoms seem predominantly colonic (eg, diarrhea) and may show reflux of barium into the terminal ileum with irregularity, nodularity, stiffness, wall thickening, and a narrowed lumen. Differential diagnoses in patients with similar radiographic findings include cancer of the cecum, ileal carcinoid, lymphoma, systemic vasculitis, radiation enteritis, ileocecal tuberculosis, and ameboma.

claims.text: Colonoscopy with biopsy (and, when possible, visualization of the terminal ileum) is recommended in the initial evaluation
claims.quote: Colonoscopy (including biopsy, sampling for enteric pathogens, and, when possible, visualization of the terminal ileum) is recommended in the initial evaluation of patients with suspected Crohn disease (3).

claims.text: Typically affects the ileum and/or colon but spares the rectum (invariably affected in ulcerative colitis); skip areas: diseased bowel sharply demarcated from adjacent normal bowel
claims.quote: Crohn disease typically affects the ileum and/or colon but spares the rectum (which is invariably affected in ulcerative colitis). Intermittent areas of diseased bowel are sharply demarcated from adjacent normal bowel (called skip areas).

claims.text: Causes Chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease that usually affects the distal ileum and colon but may occur in any part of the GI tract
claims.quote: Crohn disease is a chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease that usually affects the distal ileum and colon but may occur in any part of the gastrointestinal tract.

claims.text: Begins with crypt inflammation and abscesses → tiny focal aphthoid ulcers, which may develop into deep longitudinal and transverse ulcers with mucosal edema, giving a cobblestoned bowel
claims.quote: Crohn disease begins with crypt inflammation and abscesses, which progress to tiny focal aphthoid ulcers. These mucosal lesions may develop into deep longitudinal and transverse ulcers with intervening mucosal edema, creating a characteristic cobblestoned appearance to the bowel.

claims.text: Transmural inflammation → lymphedema and thickening of the bowel wall and mesentery; extensive inflammation may cause muscularis mucosae hypertrophy, fibrosis and stricture formation, which can lead to bowel obstruction
claims.quote: Transmural spread of inflammation leads to lymphedema and thickening of the bowel wall and mesentery. Mesenteric fat typically extends onto the serosal surface of the bowel. Mesenteric lymph nodes often enlarge. Extensive inflammation may result in hypertrophy of the muscularis mucosae, fibrosis, and stricture formation, which can lead to bowel obstruction.

claims.text: Abscesses are common and fistulas often penetrate adjoining structures (other bowel loops, bladder, psoas) and may even reach the skin; perianal fistulas and abscesses occur in 20% of cases
claims.quote: Abscesses are common, and fistulas often penetrate into adjoining structures, including other loops of bowel, the bladder, or psoas muscle. Fistulas may even extend to the skin of the anterior abdomen or flanks. Perianal fistulas and abscesses (along with other perianal findings) occur in 20% of cases, independent of the presence of intra-abdominal disease activity; these complications are frequently the most troublesome aspects of Crohn disease (1).

claims.text: Noncaseating granulomas are pathognomonic when present but are not detected in the majority of patients
claims.quote: Noncaseating granulomas can occur in lymph nodes, peritoneum, the liver, and all layers of the bowel wall. Although pathognomonic when present, granulomas are not detected in the majority of patients with Crohn disease (1, 2).

claims.text: About one-third ileum alone (ileitis), about one-third ileum and colon (right-sided predilection), about one-third colon alone (most spare the rectum)
claims.quote: About one-third of Crohn disease cases involve the ileum alone (ileitis) (4). About one-third involve the ileum and colon (ileocolitis), with a predilection for the right side of the colon. About one-third involve the colon alone (granulomatous colitis), most of which, unlike ulcerative colitis, spares the rectum.

claims.text: Symptoms Most common initial manifestations: chronic diarrhea with abdominal pain, fever, anorexia and weight loss; the abdomen is tender, and a mass or fullness may be palpable
claims.quote: The most common initial manifestations of Crohn disease are Chronic diarrhea with abdominal pain, fever, anorexia, and weight loss The abdomen is tender, and a mass or fullness may be palpable.

claims.text: Gross rectal bleeding is unusual except in isolated colonic disease; some present with an acute abdomen like appendicitis or obstruction; approximately 20 to 25% have perianal disease (especially fissures and fistulas)
claims.quote: Gross rectal bleeding is unusual except in isolated colonic disease, which may manifest similarly to ulcerative colitis. Some patients present with an acute abdomen that simulates acute appendicitis or intestinal obstruction. Approximately 20 to 25% of patients have perianal disease (especially fissures and fistulas), which is sometimes the most prominent or even initial complaint (1–3).

claims.text: Stenotic segments may cause bowel obstruction, with colicky pain, distention, obstipation and vomiting
claims.quote: Stenotic segments may cause bowel obstruction, with colicky pain, distention, obstipation, and vomiting.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: anti-TNF, biologics; mesalamine for mild
claims.quote: Anti-TNF, biologics; mesalamine for mild

claims.text: Mild disease: typically budesonide (a glucocorticoid) or sulfasalazine (an aminosalicylate)
claims.quote: Mild disease is typically managed with medications such as budesonide (a glucocorticoid) or sulfasalazine (an aminosalicylate), both of which manage inflammation.

claims.text: 5-ASA (mesalamine) should not be used in Crohn disease due to a lack of efficacy; antibiotics are not recommended for mild Crohn disease
claims.quote: 5-ASA (mesalamine) should not be used in the treatment of Crohn disease due to a lack of efficacy. Similarly, antibiotics are not recommended for the treatment of mild Crohn disease.

claims.text: Moderate to severe: typically early biologic or small molecule (sometimes with an immunomodulator) for induction, then the biologic for maintenance; systemic glucocorticoids are sometimes used for immediate relief, short-term only
claims.quote: Moderate to severe disease typically requires early introduction of a biologic agent or small molecule (sometimes in combination with an immunomodulator) for induction therapy, followed by ongoing treatment with the biologic for maintenance therapy. Systemic glucocorticoids are sometimes used for immediate symptom relief, but their use should be short-term to minimize adverse effects.

claims.text: Biologics (infliximab, adalimumab, certolizumab pegol, vedolizumab, ustekinumab, mirikizumab, risankizumab, guselkumab), with or without an immunomodulator (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate), can be first-line for induction and maintenance
claims.quote: A biologic agent (infliximab, adalimumab, certolizumab pegol, vedolizumab, ustekinumab, mirikizumab, risankizumab, guselkumab), with or without an immunomodulator (azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, or methotrexate) can be used as first-line therapy for induction and maintenance, even before a course of glucocorticoids.

claims.text: Toxic appearance, high fever, persistent vomiting, rebound, or a tender or palpable mass: hospitalize for IV fluids and antibiotics; abscesses must be drained, percutaneously or surgically
claims.quote: Patients with toxic appearance, high fever, persistent vomiting, rebound, or a tender or palpable mass must be hospitalized for administration of IV fluids and antibiotics. Abscesses must be drained, either percutaneously or surgically.

claims.text: Surgery (30 to 55% ultimately need a major operation) is best reserved for recurrent obstruction or intractable fistulas or abscesses; resection may ease symptoms but does not cure, and the disease is likely to recur
claims.quote: Even though 30 to 55% of patients ultimately require a major abdominal operation, surgery for Crohn disease is often performed reluctantly (1). It is best reserved for recurrent intestinal obstruction or intractable fistulas or abscesses. Resection of the involved bowel may ameliorate symptoms but does not cure the disease, which is likely to recur even after resection of all clinically apparent lesions.
